source.title: Open Source Sparse Autoencoders for all Residual Stream Layers of GPT2-Small

record.tranche_reason: Applies sparse autoencoders to GPT2-small residual-stream activations and reports feature sparsity and reconstruction results, extending indirect dictionary-feature evidence to this model setting; it does not reproduce the original toy-model method.
record.gate_note: The reported layerwise SAE statistics and feature examples bear on V4. The ghost-gradient and training-speed discussion does not directly test the claim. Results from commenters' separate replications are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: Trains SAEs (~25k features, 32x expansion) on all 12 GPT2-small residual-stream layers. It reports variance explained, L0 sparsity, spliced-in CE loss and anecdotal interpretable features. These bear directly on V4's claim that real models contain sparse features a dictionary can recover. It is a release post rather than a designed test, and has no toy-model or geometry component.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The author presents the SAEs as sparse, apparently interpretable and well-reconstructing, with faster training via ghost grads, LR warmup and geometric-median init. In replies he amends the reconstruction claim to 'good compared to our previous results'. He also concedes the 0.2–0.3 CE gap is a real concern, that ghost grads were buggy, and that evaluation was limited to 128-token contexts.
record.recipe_differences: Trains overcomplete sparse autoencoders on GPT2-small residual-stream activations; it does not use or reproduce the original toy-model experiment or its geometry measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Layer varies, with L0 and other summary statistics changing across layers; the post keeps the SAE expansion factor and L1 coefficient fixed. The comments and author replies discuss reconstruction evaluation at context length 128 and possible deterioration outside that context length.
record.problems: The author says the ghost-gradient implementation had an error and reports that the resulting SAEs were nevertheless good, while acknowledging that the effect of fewer features was confounded with the bug. The post says the dictionaries had not been extensively analyzed. Comments report disagreements over reconstruction CE and evaluation differences; the author discusses context length 128 and measurement issues. Feature interpretability examples are anecdotal, and no stability comparison across SAE runs is reported.
record.rows_left_out: The table's L1 loss values were not extracted because they do not directly measure the claim versions. The original-model CE entry (3.3) is recorded as the baseline for reconstruction-CE rows, not as a separate row. Commenters' independent evaluation figures and estimates were excluded because they are not results of this study.

untested.parts: No toy model, sparsity transition or geometry measurement.
No test of capacity competition or of dedicated dimensions for important features.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
No comparison across SAE runs. The author explicitly proposes training many SAEs on the same model to check stability as future work.

Only one model (GPT2-small) and only residual-stream activations. No neuron-basis spread measure, no systematic interpretability evaluation, no multi-SAE splicing, no evaluation beyond 128-token contexts.

missing.what: Context-length dependence of reconstruction: SAEs were evaluated only on 128-token contexts. Performance markedly decreases beyond that, as raised by Logan Riggs and Sam Marks and accepted in the author's replies. No numbers are given by the author.
missing.locator: Comments: Sam Marks (context length 128) and Joseph Bloom replies

missing.what: Feature density histograms showing few dense features in most layers (qualitative figure).
missing.locator: Log Feature Sparsity Histograms figure, 'How good are these Sparse AutoEncoders?'

record.verdict_notes: This is an informal release post. Its evidence for V4 is the standard 'SAE reconstructs with sparse codes' kind, with no control (e.g. SAEs on random or shuffled activations). Interpretability evidence is anecdotal. Alive-feature rows were unlinked because they describe SAE training health, not the model. Commenters' replication numbers were correctly excluded as rows, but their context-length finding was acknowledged by the author and is listed under missing.

versions.untested_parts: No toy network experiment, overcomplete-feature geometry measurement, sparsity transition, or regular-geometry test.
Does not test whether neuron polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether important features get dedicated dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or their relation to superposition.

Tests SAE-recoverable sparse features in GPT2-small residual streams, not whether the model's features are spread across neurons independently of the SAE basis, or whether this generalizes across models and context lengths.
No comparison of SAE runs or test of whether features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Does not test whether underlying features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

relationships.reason: SAEs with L0 of 12–71 out of ~25k features explain 91–99% of variance (l0-0–l0-11, vxp0–vxp11). Anecdotal dashboards show interpretable features (examples-*).
relationships.display_finding: With L0 of 12–71 out of about 25k features, the SAEs explained 91–99% of variance, and dashboards showed interpretable features anecdotally.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: The reported L0 and variance-explained values, together with anecdotal interpretable features, support sparse dictionary recovery in the tested setting.

relationships.condition: Downstream model performance with the SAE spliced in, especially later layers and contexts longer than 128 tokens
relationships.reason: CE rises from 3.3 to 3.32–3.57, worse in later layers (ce-0–ce-11). Variance explained also falls with depth (vxp0 99.15% to vxp10 91.12%). The author concedes reconstruction degrades beyond 128-token contexts (text-based).
relationships.display_finding: Cross-entropy rose from 3.3 to 3.32–3.57, worse in later layers, and variance explained fell with depth from 99.15% to 91.12%. The author concedes that reconstruction degrades beyond 128-token contexts.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Downstream model performance with the SAE spliced in, especially later layers and contexts longer than 128 tokens
source_check.reason: Individual SAE insertion increases CE, and comments report worse reconstruction beyond 128 tokens, accepted by the author. This qualifies recovery coverage and generalization; it does not negate the existence of recoverable sparse features.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
